canonical_statement: The review aims to assemble key large randomized controlled trials that established pharmacological therapies recommended or considered to improve outcomes in heart failure across the LVEF spectrum.

Trial selection was limited to studies that substantially influenced international guideline recommendations or clinical practice, with evidence organized by drug class and by reduced versus preserved LVEF where available.
The authors state that differences over time in patient characteristics, background therapy, trial design, and LVEF thresholds limit direct comparisons among the landmark trials.

Loop diuretics remain central for relief of congestion and symptoms but are not classified as classic disease-modifying, mortality-reducing therapy because well-powered randomized mortality trials are lacking.
The review concludes that ACE inhibitors reduce mortality, hospitalization, and disease progression across HFrEF, whereas evidence for disease-modifying benefit in HFpEF remains limited.

The review characterizes ARBs primarily as alternatives for patients who cannot tolerate ACE inhibitors; trials did not establish superiority over ACE inhibition, and combined ACE inhibitor plus ARB therapy raised safety concerns.
Sacubitril/valsartan is characterized as a cornerstone disease-modifying therapy in HFrEF, while its role in HFpEF is more limited and appears confined to selected subgroups.

The review cites meta-analyses showing an approximately 30%–35% relative reduction in all-cause mortality in HFrEF treated with evidence-based beta-blockers, with benefit across several clinical subgroups and reduced sudden cardiac death.

For HFmrEF, beta-blocker benefit appears smaller and rhythm-dependent; for HFpEF, the review finds no clear HF-specific prognostic advantage except when beta-blockers are indicated for comorbid conditions.

Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist trials established mortality and morbidity benefit in HFrEF, while finerenone provided evidence of benefit for worsening HF and cardiovascular death in patients with LVEF at least 40%.

The review identifies SGLT2 inhibitors as the only pharmacological class with consistent benefit across the full LVEF spectrum, with HFrEF and HFpEF trials showing reductions in HF worsening or hospitalization composites irrespective of diabetes status.
In EMPEROR-Preserved and DELIVER, the primary composite benefit was driven mainly by fewer HF events; neither trial demonstrated a significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality.

Intravenous iron is presented as a therapy that may reduce recurrent HF hospitalizations in iron-deficient HFrEF or HFmrEF, while sufficiently powered randomized outcome data in HFpEF are not available.

The review reports a pooled individual-participant analysis of VICTORIA and VICTOR in which vericiguat reduced cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization versus placebo (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.98; P=.0088).

population.label: Participants pooled from VICTORIA and VICTOR

canonical_statement: The review notes that no phase III randomized trials of vericiguat have been conducted in HFpEF; SOCRATES-PRESERVED was phase II and did not reduce NT-proBNP.
SHIFT is summarized as showing an 18% lower risk of cardiovascular death or worsening-HF hospitalization with ivabradine in symptomatic HFrEF patients in sinus rhythm on background therapy.
The DIG trial is summarized as showing no reduction in all-cause mortality with digoxin but significant reductions in HF hospitalizations and overall hospitalizations.

A prespecified pooled analysis of STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM (n=1145) is reported to favor semaglutide over placebo for a hierarchical composite of death, HF events, and timing of HF events (win ratio 1.65, 95% CI 1.42–1.91; P<.0001).

population.label: Patients with obesity-related HFpEF from STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM

concept.text: Hierarchical composite of all-cause death, number of HF events, and timing of HF events

canonical_statement: The review reports that in the LIVE trial of clinically stable HFrEF, serious cardiac events were more frequent with liraglutide than placebo (12 [10%] vs 3 [3%]; P=.04), including ventricular arrhythmia and atrial fibrillation requiring intervention.
The authors conclude that the most robust current evidence for incretin-based therapy in heart failure pertains to obesity-associated HFpEF.

The review identifies a persistent gap between guideline recommendations and real-world implementation and highlights rapid, simultaneous initiation or uptitration of guideline-directed therapy as an evidence-supported implementation strategy.

The authors emphasize under-representation of women, older adults, socioeconomically disadvantaged patients, and patients with advanced comorbidities in heart-failure trials as an important evidence and implementation gap.

The review concludes that contemporary HFrEF therapy is supported by multiple complementary disease-modifying drug classes, while future priorities include closing implementation gaps, improving trial representation, developing new therapies, and advancing precision medicine.
The article states that it generated or analyzed no original data and therefore has no data available for sharing.
